title: An 88-day eccentric model gives a conditional duration-bin tail fraction of 0.093 for HD 139139
abstract: We test a restricted eccentric-orbit explanation for the known HD 139139 dips. Under a solar host, small objects and complete detection, an eight-bin duration fit with period at least 88.1 days gives eccentricity 0.874 and score 11.50. A free-period fit gives 10.69. A conditional 999-sample diagnostic gives tail fraction 0.093. Wider bins and suspect-event removal retain the null result. This diagnostic does not exclude the restricted long-period model. The simulation uses fitted parameters and a finite candidate rule; it is not a uniform confidence test. Selection, exact geometry, pixel defects and independent confirmation remain open. No new dip or planet is found. Source records stay external. Original code, aggregate evidence, a figure and exact retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Duration-bin counts and model predictions under a solar-host assumption. These fits do not confirm an orbital source.
